text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:

- At a seminar on Switzerland's role during World War Two, World Jewish Congress assistant secretary general Maram Stern said that efforts should focus on transparency regarding the assets of Jewish Holocaust victims.
- Neue Zuercher Zeitung group reported a 1996 net profit of 15.2 million Swiss francs, down from 19.5 million in the previous year.
- Switzerland remains second-richest country in the World measured by per capita income, according to a study by the World Bank.

- Some 100 skinheads chanting Nazi slogans intimidated pedestrians. Three young people were injured by the group. The President of the Radical Democrats Franz Steinegger demanded the resignation of Zurich's police department chief Robert Neukomm, after he was quoted saying that Jean-Pascal Delmuraz and Christoph Blocher legitimized extreme rightist activities with their recent comments and speeches.
- Swiss charter airline TEA reported a 1996 net profit of two million Swiss francs, down from 5.6 million in 1995. Sales rose by 17 percent to 120 million francs.
- Largest Swiss travel group Kuoni plans to introduce night flights to holiday destinations on the Mediterranean in a bid to increase its market leadership.
- Swiss citizens regard deregulation of the Swiss insurance market 'rather negatively', a Vox opinion poll showed.
- Swiss Federal Rail president Benedikt Weibel said that a new rail tunnel through the Loetschberg may be preferable as geological tests at the Gotthard showed some severe probelms.
